line.placeZoomed: Where on the number line is the number? Tap there.
line.tipZoomed: The number line is zoomed in: each mark is {step}.
line.placeDouble: The whole, 100 %, is {total} kr. Where on the line is {kr} kr?
line.tipDouble: What percent of {total} kr is it? Each mark is 5 %.
line.placeEnds: The film starts at {t} and lasts {d}. Where on the timeline does it end?
line.tipTime: Each mark is a quarter of an hour, 15 minutes.
line.tipEnds: Go forward an hour at a time, then the quarters.
grid.why.scaledCount: You've coloured {k} squares – the figure twice as big has {n}.
grid.why.shape: The right number of squares, but the shape isn't right – compare with the original.
grid.why.notOnLine: The points aren't both on the line – put in x and work out y.
grid.enlarge.prompt: Draw the figure twice as big (scale 2:1) in the empty part of the grid.
grid.enlarge.tip: Each square of the figure becomes 2 × 2 squares.
grid.enlarge.explain: The figure has {n} squares. Twice as big it has {m} – each square becomes four.
grid.line.prompt: Draw the line {f}: mark two points on it.
grid.line.tip: Choose an x and work out y. Do the same with another x.
grid.line.explain: For example x = 0 gives y = {m}, and each step right changes y by {k}.
grid.line.whySign: The line slopes the wrong way – check the sign of k.
grid.line.whyM: The line crosses the y-axis in the wrong place – check m.
grid.turn.left: Turn the triangle a quarter turn anticlockwise about the origin. Mark the new triangle's corners.
grid.turn.right: Turn the triangle a quarter turn clockwise about the origin. Mark the new triangle's corners.
grid.turn.half: Turn the triangle a half turn about the origin. Mark the new triangle's corners.
grid.turn.tipQuarter: A quarter turn anticlockwise: (x, y) becomes (−y, x). Clockwise: (y, −x). One corner at a time.
grid.turn.explain.left: Each corner (x, y) goes to (−y, x).
grid.turn.whyDirection: The wrong way – anticlockwise is the other way from a clock's hands.
grid.turn.whyReflect: That's a reflection, not a rotation.
sort.venn.prompt: Sort the numbers into the Venn diagram.
sort.venn.tip: Test each number: can it be divided by {a}? By {b}?
sort.venn.explain: Numbers divisible by both {a} and {b} go in the middle – like {ab}.
sort.quad.rightAngles: Does the quadrilateral have four right angles?
sort.quad.parallel: Does the quadrilateral have two pairs of parallel sides?
sort.quad.equalSides: Does the quadrilateral have four equal sides?
sort.quad.tip.rightAngles: Compare the corners with the corner of a sheet of paper.
sort.quad.tip.parallel: Parallel sides go the same way and never meet.
sort.quad.explain.rightAngles: The square and the rectangle have four right angles.
sort.quad.explain.parallel: Square, rectangle, rhombus and parallelogram have two pairs of parallel sides.
sort.quad.explain.equalSides: The square and the rhombus have four equal sides.
sort.why.quad.rightAngles.yes: This is {name}, which has four right angles.
sort.why.quad.rightAngles.no: This is {name}, which doesn't have four right angles.
sort.why.quad.parallel.yes: This is {name}, which has two pairs of parallel sides.
sort.why.quad.parallel.no: This is {name}, which doesn't have two pairs of parallel sides.
sort.why.quad.equalSides.yes: This is {name}, which has four equal sides.
sort.why.quad.equalSides.no: This is {name}, which doesn't have four equal sides.
sort.events.prompt: The bag has the marbles in the picture. Put them in order from impossible to certain.
sort.events.tip: If the colour isn't in the bag, it's impossible. If every marble is like that, it's certain. More marbles of a colour – a bigger chance.
sort.events.explain: No marble is {none}: impossible. More are {many} than {few}. All are {many} or {few}: certain.
sort.program.prompt: Put the lines in order so the program prints {r}.
sort.program.tip: A variable has to get a value before it's used.
sort.program.explain: Each line uses what the line before did – in that order the program prints {r}.
sort.solution.prompt: Put the solution in order, from the equation to the answer.
sort.solution.tip: Each line comes from the line before: one step at a time, the same on both sides.
sort.solution.explain: From the equation, one step at a time, to x = {x}.
choice.protractor.tipRight: The first arm points right – read the scale with 0 there.
choice.protractor.tipLeft: The first arm points left – read the scale with 0 there.
choice.protractor.explain: Read {scale}, with 0 at the first arm: {d}°.
choice.protractor.whyScale: You read the wrong scale – use the one with 0 at the first arm.
choice.protractor.whyTens: Read carefully – count the tens on the scale.
choice.congruent.prompt: Which triangle is congruent to the one above?
choice.congruent.tip: Congruent figures have exactly the same measures – they may be turned or mirrored.
choice.congruent.explain: The same sides, {a}, {b} and {c} – just turned or flipped.
choice.congruent.whySimilar: The same shape but twice as big – similar, not congruent.
choice.congruent.whyOneSide: One side isn't the same length.
choice.paper.prompt: What is the area, counted in squares?
choice.paper.tipTriangle: A triangle is half the rectangle round it: base · height / 2.
choice.paper.tipParallelogram: Cut off a triangle and move it – the parallelogram becomes a rectangle: base · height.
choice.paper.whyWhole: That's the whole rectangle – the triangle is half.
choice.paper.whyCount: Count again – two half squares make a whole.
choice.paper.whyAdd: Area is base times height, not plus.
choice.paper.whyHalfParallelogram: A parallelogram isn't a triangle – base · height, without halving.
choice.paper.whyBox: That's the rectangle round it – the slanted corners aren't part of it.
choice.net.which: Which net folds into a cube?
choice.net.whichNot: Which net can NOT fold into a cube?
choice.net.tip: A cube has six faces. Imagine folding the faces up round a bottom.
choice.net.explain: A cube net has six squares, never four in a 2 × 2 block and never five in a row.
choice.net.whyBlock: Four squares in a 2 × 2 block would land on top of each other.
choice.net.whyRow: Six in a row go round the cube – two faces double up and two are missing.
choice.net.whyFive: Five in a row: folding, two faces land on top of each other.
choice.net.whyFolds: This net does fold into a cube.
choice.reasonable.price: Pick-and-mix costs {p} kr/kg. You buy {kg} kg. Which price is reasonable?
choice.reasonable.tip: Round the numbers and work it out in your head.
choice.reasonable.whyBig: Estimate: about {e}. This is ten times too much.
choice.reasonable.whySmall: Estimate: about {e}. This is ten times too little.
choice.reasonable.whyAdd: That's the numbers added – it should be times.
choice.factors.prompt: Which is the number's prime factorisation?
choice.factors.tip: Divide by the smallest prime that goes, again and again.
choice.factors.explain: {n} = {f}, and all the factors are primes.
choice.factors.whyNotPrime: {f} isn't a prime – split it up.
choice.sale.prompt: A jacket costs {k} kr. It's on sale at {p} % off. What does it cost now?
choice.sale.tip: {p} % off: you pay {f} of the price.
choice.sale.whyOff: That's the discount – what does the jacket cost?
choice.sale.whyKronor: The discount is {p} percent, not {p} kronor.
choice.sale.whyUp: A sale makes it cheaper, not dearer.
choice.vat.add: The price without VAT is {k} kr. VAT is 25 %. What is the price with VAT?
choice.vat.remove: The price with 25 % VAT is {k} kr. What is the price without VAT?
choice.vat.tipRemove: The price with VAT is 1.25 times the price without. Divide by 1.25.
choice.vat.explainRemove: {k} / 1.25 = {r} kr – and 25 % of {r} kr added makes {k} kr again.
choice.vat.whyDown: VAT is added – the price goes up.
choice.vat.whyQuarter: The VAT was 25 % of the price without VAT – not of {k} kr. Divide by 1.25 instead.
choice.loan.amortise: You borrow {k} kr and pay back the same each month for {y} year(s). How much do you repay each month?
choice.loan.tipAmortise: Split the loan over all the months: {m} months.
choice.loan.interest: You have a loan of {k} kr at {r} % interest a year. How much interest do you pay in the first month?
choice.loan.tipInterest: Work out a year's interest and divide by 12.
choice.loan.explainInterest: {r} % of {k} kr is {y} kr in a year. A month: {y} / 12 = {m} kr.
choice.loan.whyAll: That's the whole loan – it's split over the months.
choice.loan.whyYear: That's per year – divide by 12 too.
choice.loan.whyOneYear: That would be for a one-year loan – it's over {y} years.
choice.litres.prompt: How many litres does the box hold?
choice.litres.tip: 1 dm³ = 1 litre. Work out the volume in dm³.
choice.litres.tipCm: Change to dm first: 10 cm = 1 dm. Then 1 dm³ = 1 litre.
choice.litres.explainCm: {lw} dm · {ww} dm · {hw} dm = {v} dm³, which is {v} litres.
choice.litres.whyAdd: The volume is length · width · height – not plus.
choice.litres.whyBase: That's only the base – times the height too.
choice.litres.whySurface: That's the surface area – the volume is length · width · height.
choice.litres.whyCm: Cubic centimetres aren't litres: 1,000 cm³ = 1 litre.
